name: Auto Version on Main

on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID:
        required: true
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY:
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Generate GitHub App Token
        id: generate-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Configure Git
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.generate_token.outputs.app-slug }}
          APP_ID: ${{ steps.get-user-id.outputs.user-id }}
        run: |
          git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/".insteadOf https://github.com/
          git config --global user.name '${APP_SLUG}[bot]'
          git config --global user.email '${APP_ID}+${APP_SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'

      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Get current version
        id: current-version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          echo "version=$CURRENT_VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Current version: $CURRENT_VERSION"

      - name: Determine version bump
        id: bump
        run: |
          # Get commit messages since last tag
          LAST_TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "")

          if [ -z "$LAST_TAG" ]; then
            # No tags yet, get all commits
            COMMITS=$(git log --pretty=format:"%s" HEAD)
          else
            COMMITS=$(git log --pretty=format:"%s" ${LAST_TAG}..HEAD)
          fi

          echo "Analyzing commits:"
          echo "$COMMITS"

          # Determine bump type based on conventional commits
          if echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(feat|feature)(\(.+\))?!:|^BREAKING CHANGE:"; then
            BUMP="major"
          elif echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(feat|feature)(\(.+\))?:"; then
            BUMP="minor"
          elif echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore)(\(.+\))?:"; then
            BUMP="patch"
          else
            BUMP="patch"
          fi

          echo "bump=$BUMP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Version bump type: $BUMP"

      - name: Calculate new version
        id: new-version
        env:
          CURRENT_VERSION: ${{ steps.current-version.outputs.version }}
          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.bump }}
        run: |
          CURRENT="${CURRENT_VERSION}"
          BUMP="${BUMP_TYPE}"

          # Split version into parts
          IFS='.' read -ra VERSION_PARTS <<< "$CURRENT"
          MAJOR="${VERSION_PARTS[0]}"
          MINOR="${VERSION_PARTS[1]}"
          PATCH="${VERSION_PARTS[2]}"

          # Increment based on bump type
          case $BUMP in
            major)
              MAJOR=$((MAJOR + 1))
              MINOR=0
              PATCH=0
              ;;
            minor)
              MINOR=$((MINOR + 1))
              PATCH=0
              ;;
            patch)
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              ;;
          esac

          NEW_VERSION="${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "New version: $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Update package.json version
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          npm version "${NEW_VERSION}" --no-git-tag-version
          echo "Updated package.json to version $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Commit version bump
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          git add package.json
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to ${NEW_VERSION} [skip ci]" || echo "No changes to commit"

      - name: Create and push tag
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          git tag -a "v${NEW_VERSION}" -m "Release version ${NEW_VERSION}"
          git push origin main
          git push origin "v${NEW_VERSION}"
          echo "Created and pushed tag v${NEW_VERSION}"

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ steps.bump.output.bump }}
        run: |
          gh release create "v${NEW_VERSION}" \
            --title "Release v${NEW_VERSION}" \
            --notes "## Changes in v${NEW_VERSION}

          This release was automatically generated from commits to main.

          **Version bump type**: ${BUMP}"

name: Release Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  AWS_REGION: eu-west-2
  NODE_VERSION: '20'

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Version
    uses: ./.github/workflows/version.yml

      contents: write
      id-token: write
    secrets:
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID }}
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY }}

  deploy-dev:
    name: Deploy to dev
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev
    outputs:
      codebuild-project: ${{ steps.get-outputs.outputs.codebuild-project }}
      source-bucket: ${{ steps.get-outputs.outputs.source-bucket }}
      source-path: ${{ steps.get-outputs.outputs.source-path }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup pnpm
        run: |
          npm install -g pnpm@latest-10
          pnpm install

      - name: Setup NODE_VERSION
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm i --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Configure AWS Credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@56d6a583f00f6bad6d19d91d53a7bc3b8143d0e9 # v5.1.1
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.DEV_DEPLOYMENT_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Deploy CDK stack to dev
        run: npx nx run cdk:deploy:dev

      - name: Get Stack outputs
        id: get-outputs
        working-directory: cdk
        run: |
          CODEBUILD_PROJECT=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name dev-e2e --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='CodeBuildProjectName'].OutputValue" --output text)
          echo "codebuild-project=${CODEBUILD_PROJECT}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "COdebuild Project: ${CODEBUILD_PROJECT}"
          SOURCE_BUCKET=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name dev-e2e --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='SourceBucketName'].OutputValue" --output text)
          echo "source-bucket=${SOURCE_BUCKET}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Source Bucket: ${SOURCE_BUCKET}"
          SOURCE_PATH=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name dev-e2e --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='SourcePath'].OutputValue" --output text)
          echo "source-path=${SOURCE_PATH}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Source Path: ${SOURCE_PATH}"

  e2e-dev:
    name: E2E tests on dev
    needs: deploy-dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.ref_name }}

      - name: Setup pnpm
        run: |
          npm install -g pnpm@latest-10
          pnpm install

      - name: Setup NODE_VERSION
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm i --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Configure AWS Credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@56d6a583f00f6bad6d19d91d53a7bc3b8143d0e9 # v5.1.1
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.DEV_DEPLOYMENT_ROLE }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Upload source to S3
        env:
          SOURCE_BUCKET: ${{ needs.deploy-dev.outputs.source-bucket }}
          SOURCE_PATH: ${{ needs.deploy-dev.outputs.source-path }}
        run: |
          echo "UPLOADING source to s3 get store path"
          STORE_PATH=$(pnpm store path)
          pnpm store prune

          mkdir -p .pnpm-store
          cp -r "${STORE_PATH}"/* .pnpm-store/

          echo "UPLOADING source to s3 for e2e"
          zip -rqy source.zip . -x '.git/*' -x ',.nx/*' -x "cdk/cdk.out/*"
          aws s3 cp source.zip "s3://${SOURCE_BUCKET}/${SOURCE_PATH}"

      - name: Trigger Codebuild and wait for completion
        id: codebuild
        env:
          CODEBUILD_PROJECT: ${{ needs.deploy-dev.outputs.codebuild-project }}
        run: |
          echo "Starting Codebuild project: ${CODEBUILD_PROJECT}"

          # Start Build
          BUILD_ID=$(aws codebuild start-build --project-name "${CODEBUILD_PROJECT}" --query 'build.id' --output text)

          echo "Build started ${BUILD_ID}"
          echo "build-id=${BUILD_ID}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # poll for completion
          while true; do
            BUILD_STATUS=$(aws codebuild batch-get-builds --ids "${BUILD_ID}" --query 'builds[0].buildStatus' --output text)
            CURRENT_PHASE=$(aws codebuild batch-get-builds --ids "${BUILD_ID}" --query 'builds[0].currentPhase' --output text)

            echo "Build status: ${BUILD_STATUS}, phase: ${CURRENT_PHASE}"

            case "${BUILD_STATUS}" in
              SUCCEEDED)
                echo "E2E tests passed!"
                exit 0
                ;;
              FAILED|FAULT|STOPPED|TIMED_OUT)
                echo "E2E tests failed with status &{BUILD_STATUS}"

                # get build logs
                BUILD_ARN=$(aws codebuild batch-get-builds --ids "${BUILD_ID}" --query 'builds[0].arn' --output text)
                echo "Build logs: https://${AWS_REGION}.console.aws.amazon.com/codesuite/codebuild/projects/${CODEBUILD_PROJECT}/build/${BUILD_ID}"

                exit 1
                ;;
              IN_PROGRESS)
                sleep 30
                ;;
              *)
                echo "unknown status: ${BUILD_STATUS}"
                sleep 30
                ;;
            esac
          done

          echo "source-bucket=${SOURCE_BUCKET}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

name: Auto Version on Main

on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID:
        required: true
      GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY:
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Generate GitHub App Token
        id: generate-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.GH_UDPTAGRELEASE_GOVUK_ONCE_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Configure Git
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.generate_token.outputs.app-slug }}
          APP_ID: ${{ steps.get-user-id.outputs.user-id }}
        run: |
          git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/".insteadOf https://github.com/
          git config --global user.name '${APP_SLUG}[bot]'
          git config --global user.email '${APP_ID}+${APP_SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'

      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Get current version
        id: current-version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          echo "version=$CURRENT_VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Current version: $CURRENT_VERSION"

      - name: Determine version bump
        id: bump
        run: |
          # Get commit messages since last tag
          LAST_TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "")

          if [ -z "$LAST_TAG" ]; then
            # No tags yet, get all commits
            COMMITS=$(git log --pretty=format:"%s" HEAD)
          else
            COMMITS=$(git log --pretty=format:"%s" ${LAST_TAG}..HEAD)
          fi

          echo "Analyzing commits:"
          echo "$COMMITS"

          # Determine bump type based on conventional commits
          if echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(feat|feature)(\(.+\))?!:|^BREAKING CHANGE:"; then
            BUMP="major"
          elif echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(feat|feature)(\(.+\))?:"; then
            BUMP="minor"
          elif echo "$COMMITS" | grep -qE "^(fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore)(\(.+\))?:"; then
            BUMP="patch"
          else
            BUMP="patch"
          fi

          echo "bump=$BUMP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Version bump type: $BUMP"

      - name: Calculate new version
        id: new-version
        env:
          CURRENT_VERSION: ${{ steps.current-version.outputs.version }}
          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.bump }}
        run: |
          CURRENT="${CURRENT_VERSION}"
          BUMP="${BUMP_TYPE}"

          # Split version into parts
          IFS='.' read -ra VERSION_PARTS <<< "$CURRENT"
          MAJOR="${VERSION_PARTS[0]}"
          MINOR="${VERSION_PARTS[1]}"
          PATCH="${VERSION_PARTS[2]}"

          # Increment based on bump type
          case $BUMP in
            major)
              MAJOR=$((MAJOR + 1))
              MINOR=0
              PATCH=0
              ;;
            minor)
              MINOR=$((MINOR + 1))
              PATCH=0
              ;;
            patch)
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              ;;
          esac

          NEW_VERSION="${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "New version: $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Update package.json version
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          npm version "${NEW_VERSION}" --no-git-tag-version
          echo "Updated package.json to version $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Commit version bump
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          git add package.json
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to ${NEW_VERSION} [skip ci]" || echo "No changes to commit"

      - name: Create and push tag
        env:
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          git tag -a "v${NEW_VERSION}" -m "Release version ${NEW_VERSION}"
          git push origin main
          git push origin "v${NEW_VERSION}"
          echo "Created and pushed tag v${NEW_VERSION}"

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.generate-token.outputs.token }}
          NEW_VERSION: ${{ steps.new-version.outputs.version }}
          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ steps.bump.output.bump }}
        run: |
          gh release create "v${NEW_VERSION}" \
            --title "Release v${NEW_VERSION}" \
            --notes "## Changes in v${NEW_VERSION}

          This release was automatically generated from commits to main.

          **Version bump type**: ${BUMP}"

## The Problem

Your release pipeline (`version.yml`) is failing because an **org-level ruleset now requires signed commits** on the `main` branch. Here's what's happening:

1. When code merges to `main`, the release workflow runs
2. The version workflow bumps `package.json`, creates a **local git commit** (`git commit -m "chore: bump version..."`)
3. It tries to `git push origin main` — but the org ruleset **rejects the push** because that commit isn't cryptographically signed

The bot's commits used to go through fine, but the org added (or enforced) a commit signing requirement, and unsigned commits are now blocked.

## The Fix: Use GitHub's API Instead of `git commit` + `git push`

Commits created through the **GitHub REST API** (the Git Data API) are **automatically signed/verified by GitHub itself**. This is a documented behavior — GitHub treats API-created commits the same as web UI commits, signing them with GitHub's own key.

So instead of:
```
npm version → git add → git commit → git push   (unsigned, rejected)
```

We do:
```
npm version → create blob via API → create tree → create commit → update ref
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
              All via gh api — GitHub signs the commit automatically ✅
```

## Bonus Bugs in the Current Workflow

While reading `version.yml`, I also found these pre-existing bugs in the "Configure Git" step (lines 26-34):

| Line | Bug | Impact |
|------|-----|--------|
| 29 | `steps.generate_token` (underscore) — step ID is `generate-token` (hyphen) | `APP_SLUG` is always empty |
| 30 | `steps.get-user-id` — no such step exists | `APP_ID` is always empty |
| 33-34 | Single quotes `'${APP_SLUG}[bot]'` prevent shell variable expansion | Git author is literally the string `${APP_SLUG}[bot]` |
| 147 | `steps.bump.output.bump` — should be `outputs` (plural) | `BUMP_TYPE` is empty in release notes |

These didn't cause visible failures before because the push still went through (the URL rewrite on line 32 handled auth, and git doesn't care about author name for push permissions). But they mean the commit metadata was wrong.

## What I'm Changing

1. **Remove** the broken "Configure Git" step entirely (not needed when using the API)
2. **Replace** the "Commit version bump" + "Create and push tag" steps with a single step that uses `gh api` to create the commit, update the branch ref, and create the tag — all via the API, so GitHub signs everything
3. **Fix** the typo in the GitHub Release step (`output` → `outputs`)

## The Process

The discussion outlines creating signed commits by:

3. **Updating a Reference** - Pointing the branch to the new commit SHA

## Documentation

Here are the key references:

1. **[About commit signature verification - GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification)**: "GitHub will automatically use GPG to sign commits you make using the web interface."

2. **[How to Use Commit Signing with GitHub Apps - Community Discussion #50055](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/50055)**: This is the most relevant one. It confirms:
   > "Using a GitHub App Installation token will skip the need to specify a GPG Key, instead GitHub will sign the commit using their GPG Key through the GitHub App."
   
   And critically:
   > "You need to use the tree API to have it signed" — standard git CLI operations with installation tokens do **not** produce verified commits, only API-based tree operations do.

3. **[Automatically sign commits from GitHub Actions using the REST API](https://gist.github.com/swinton/03e84635b45c78353b1f71e41007fc7c)**: A gist showing the exact pattern (create blob → create tree → create commit → update ref).

## Can You Test via a Branch?

Yes, but with a caveat. The version workflow is a **reusable workflow** called from `release.yml`, which only triggers on `push` to `main`. To test it:

**Option A** — Modify `release.yml` temporarily to trigger on your branch:
```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - support  # temporary for testing
```
Then the version step would need to push to `support` instead of `main`. This requires a few more tweaks.

**Option B** — Test the API calls manually from your terminal using `gh api` with a personal token against a test branch. This validates that the API creates verified commits without touching the main pipeline.

**Option C** — Create a separate test workflow on the `support` branch that runs the API-based version logic against `support`.
